To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ESR1 rs3798577 and other SNPs may be involved in cancers development.
estrogen receptor alpha gene polymorphisms may play a role in the development of breast cancer, colon cancer, bladder cancer, hepatocellular cancer and acute myelogenous leukemia.
ESR1 gene variants are associated with the development of several types of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of estrogen receptor gene alpha in cancer development.
the identification of the genetic factors that contribute to breast cancer susceptibility, and to understand the mechanisms of breast cancer pathogenesis.
the role of ESR1 polymorphism in the development and prognosis of cancer and may contribute to the identification of new molecular targets for cancer therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polymorphism rs3798577 is the most interesting marker to be investigated in future studies.
the ESR1 polymorphic variants are not the main determinants of the susceptibility to the development of breast cancer, but they may contribute to the risk of other malignancies.
estrogen receptor alpha SNPs rs3798577, rs2077647, rs1801132 and rs2228480 may have some influence in the susceptibility to cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polymorphisms rs3798577, rs2228480 and rs2077647 are promising candidates to be included in cancer susceptibility models.
the estrogen receptor gene polymorphisms are associated with cancer risk, however the risk alleles differ according to tumor site.
estrogen receptor gene alpha SNPs may be associated with cancer risk and further studies are needed to confirm the associations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
estrogen receptor polymorphisms may influence the risk of cancers.
the association between ESR1 polymorphism and cancer risk is not straightforward and may depend on the type of the malignancy and/or on the ethnicity.
estrogen receptor alpha polymorphisms may contribute to cancers risk.
